findings.snippet: private_key      = "[REDACTED PRIVATE KEY]" # vuln-code-snippet vuln-line iacLeakedKeyChallenge
findings.pci_dss: Req 8.3.2 - Strong cryptography for credential management
findings.description: Private key material in source code.
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized service access, data breach, and regulatory violation. Credentials in VCS history persist even after removal from HEAD. Rotation is mandatory and git history must be purged.
remediation: Remove all hardcoded credentials immediately.
Store secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager).
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
Scan git history (truffleHog, gitleaks) and revoke previously committed secrets.
Add pre-commit hooks (detect-secrets) to prevent future leakage.

findings.title: MD5 Usage
findings.snippet: export const hash = (data: string) => crypto.createHash('md5').update(data).digest('hex')
findings.pci_dss: Req 6.2.4 - Prevent use of broken cryptographic algorithms
findings.iso27001: A.10.1.1 Policy on the Use of Cryptographic Controls
findings.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken.
findings.business_impact: Cryptographic bypass enabling password cracking, data integrity violation, and authentication compromise. PCI DSS Req 6.2.4 and NIST SP 800-131A violation.
remediation: Replace MD5/SHA-1 with SHA-256 or SHA-3 for non-password hashing and integrity use cases.
For password storage, use a password-hashing function such as Argon2id, bcrypt, or scrypt; never use MD5/SHA-1.
For encryption, use an authenticated mode such as AES-256-GCM with keys managed outside source code.
Add regression tests that reject deprecated algorithms in security-sensitive code paths.

rule_contract.title: MD5 Usage
rule_contract.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken.

remediation: Replace MD5 with SHA-256 or a stronger modern hash when hashing is required for integrity or non-password data.
For password storage, use a dedicated password-hashing scheme such as Argon2id or bcrypt with an appropriate work factor.
Do not use MD5 for authentication, password storage, signatures, or security-sensitive integrity decisions.
Add regression tests verifying the selected algorithm and rejecting legacy MD5 usage in security-sensitive code paths.

findings.description: Enterprise static control matched: Node Unsafe eval/vm/new Function.
findings.business_impact: Arbitrary code execution, full system compromise.
remediation: Remove eval(), new Function(), vm.runIn*(), or equivalent dynamic execution from request-controlled paths.
Use JSON.parse() or a schema validator for data; do not turn input strings into executable JavaScript.
If dynamic behavior is unavoidable, allow-list the supported operations and map them to fixed functions.
Add regression tests proving crafted expressions are rejected and cannot execute code.

remediation: Remove eval(), vm execution and new Function() for untrusted input.
Use schema-validated data, safe interpreters or fixed allow-listed commands.
Apply CSP and runtime sandboxing where dynamic execution cannot be avoided.

findings.description: Source-to-sink indicator: req. reaches fetch( near the same function/block.
findings.business_impact: Internal service access, metadata exposure (AWS IMDS), SSRF pivot to RCE, lateral movement.
remediation: Allow outbound requests only to an explicit server-side destination allow-list; never trust a client-supplied URL by itself.
Resolve the destination and validate every resulting IP address, including IPv4, IPv6, loopback, link-local, private, and cloud-metadata ranges.
Re-validate the destination after DNS resolution and after redirects; prevent DNS-rebinding and redirect-based allow-list bypasses.
Allow only required URL schemes, use a controlled egress proxy where possible, and block direct access to internal management and metadata endpoints.
Add regression tests for private IPs, IPv6, encoded/alternate IP forms, redirects, DNS rebinding, and cloud metadata addresses.

remediation: Validate all outbound URLs against a server-side allow-list of trusted hosts.
Block requests to private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x).
Use a dedicated HTTP proxy that enforces egress filtering.
Disable unnecessary URL schemes (file://, gopher://, dict://).
Never forward raw user-supplied URLs to backend HTTP clients.

findings.pci_dss: Req 8.3.2 - Strong cryptography for credential management
findings.description: Private key material in source code.
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized service access, data breach, and regulatory violation. Credentials in VCS history persist even after removal from HEAD. Rotation is mandatory and git history must be purged.
remediation: Remove all hardcoded credentials immediately.
Store secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager).
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
Scan git history (truffleHog, gitleaks) and revoke previously committed secrets.
Add pre-commit hooks (detect-secrets) to prevent future leakage.

findings.snippet: eval(
findings.description: Enterprise static control matched: Node Unsafe eval/vm/new Function.
findings.business_impact: Arbitrary code execution, full system compromise.
remediation: Remove eval(), new Function(), vm.runIn*(), or equivalent dynamic execution from request-controlled paths.
Use JSON.parse() or a schema validator for data; do not turn input strings into executable JavaScript.
If dynamic behavior is unavoidable, allow-list the supported operations and map them to fixed functions.
Add regression tests proving crafted expressions are rejected and cannot execute code.

Apply CSP and runtime sandboxing where dynamic execution cannot be avoided.

findings.title: Login Brute Force Rate Limit Missing
findings.snippet: app.post('/rest/user/login', login())
findings.description: Abuse-prone login endpoint appears without nearby rate-limit, replay, lockout, or idempotency controls.
remediation: Add a server-side rate limit appropriate to this endpoint: per-account and per-IP, and per-tenant where applicable.
For login/OTP/reset flows, add progressive backoff and temporary blocking after repeated failures; do not rely on client-side throttling.
For payment, checkout, coupon, and other duplicate-sensitive actions, require an idempotency key and enforce it in the server-side transaction.
Return 429 when throttled, emit abuse metrics, and alert on repeated failures or abnormal request velocity.
Add automated tests for burst traffic, replayed requests, duplicate submissions, and lockout/backoff behavior.
findings.pci_dss: Req 6.2.4 / Req 8 - Abuse prevention and authentication controls
findings.control_gap_basis: Concrete server-side route definition was identified; no matching rate-limit, throttle, lockout, replay-protection, or idempotency control was detected in the route declaration or applicable nearby middleware context.

rule_contract.title: Login Brute Force Rate Limit Missing
rule_contract.description: Abuse-prone login endpoint appears without nearby rate-limit, replay, lockout, or idempotency controls.

remediation: Apply server-side rate limits per account and source IP; scope limits by tenant where applicable.
Use progressive backoff or bounded temporary blocking after repeated failures and return HTTP 429 when throttled.
Do not reveal whether an account exists in authentication error responses.
Add tests for burst, distributed, and repeated login attempts plus recovery behavior.

grouped.title: MD5 Usage
grouped.pci_dss: Req 6.2.4 - Prevent use of broken cryptographic algorithms
grouped.iso27001: A.10.1.1 Policy on the Use of Cryptographic Controls
grouped.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken.
grouped.business_impact: Cryptographic bypass enabling password cracking, data integrity violation, and authentication compromise. PCI DSS Req 6.2.4 and NIST SP 800-131A violation.
remediation: Replace MD5/SHA-1 with SHA-256 or SHA-3 for non-password hashing and integrity use cases.
For password storage, use a password-hashing function such as Argon2id, bcrypt, or scrypt; never use MD5/SHA-1.
For encryption, use an authenticated mode such as AES-256-GCM with keys managed outside source code.
Add regression tests that reject deprecated algorithms in security-sensitive code paths.

rule_contract.title: MD5 Usage
rule_contract.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken.

remediation: Replace MD5 with SHA-256 or a stronger modern hash when hashing is required for integrity or non-password data.
For password storage, use a dedicated password-hashing scheme such as Argon2id or bcrypt with an appropriate work factor.
Do not use MD5 for authentication, password storage, signatures, or security-sensitive integrity decisions.
Add regression tests verifying the selected algorithm and rejecting legacy MD5 usage in security-sensitive code paths.

grouped.title: SSRF Dynamic Outbound Request
grouped.description: Source-to-sink indicator: req. reaches fetch( near the same function/block.
grouped.business_impact: Internal service access, metadata exposure (AWS IMDS), SSRF pivot to RCE, lateral movement.
remediation: Allow outbound requests only to an explicit server-side destination allow-list; never trust a client-supplied URL by itself.
Resolve the destination and validate every resulting IP address, including IPv4, IPv6, loopback, link-local, private, and cloud-metadata ranges.
Re-validate the destination after DNS resolution and after redirects; prevent DNS-rebinding and redirect-based allow-list bypasses.
Allow only required URL schemes, use a controlled egress proxy where possible, and block direct access to internal management and metadata endpoints.
Add regression tests for private IPs, IPv6, encoded/alternate IP forms, redirects, DNS rebinding, and cloud metadata addresses.

rule_contract.title: SSRF Dynamic Outbound Request
rule_contract.description: Source-to-sink indicator: req. reaches fetch( near the same function/block.

remediation: Validate all outbound URLs against a server-side allow-list of trusted hosts.
Block requests to private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x).
Use a dedicated HTTP proxy that enforces egress filtering.
Disable unnecessary URL schemes (file://, gopher://, dict://).
Never forward raw user-supplied URLs to backend HTTP clients.

grouped.title: eval() Call
grouped.description: Enterprise static control matched: Node Unsafe eval/vm/new Function.
grouped.business_impact: Arbitrary code execution, full system compromise.
remediation: Remove eval(), new Function(), vm.runIn*(), or equivalent dynamic execution from request-controlled paths.
Use JSON.parse() or a schema validator for data; do not turn input strings into executable JavaScript.
If dynamic behavior is unavoidable, allow-list the supported operations and map them to fixed functions.
Add regression tests proving crafted expressions are rejected and cannot execute code.

rule_contract.title: eval() Call
rule_contract.description: Enterprise static control matched: Node Unsafe eval/vm/new Function.

remediation: Remove eval(), vm execution and new Function() for untrusted input.
Use schema-validated data, safe interpreters or fixed allow-listed commands.
Apply CSP and runtime sandboxing where dynamic execution cannot be avoided.

attack_paths.title: Attack Path: SSRF Dynamic Outbound Request
attack_paths.narrative: A SSRF Dynamic Outbound Request finding (CWE-918) traces from req. to fetch( across 1 hop. Both endpoints were observed in the finding's own taint path, so the reachability of this chain is established by static analysis. Observed at routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:24. This does NOT assert that the chain is exploitable in a live environment: transport, deployment and upstream validation are separate questions this scan does not answer.

sbom.name: express-jwt

vulnerabilities.details:
### Overview
Versions before and including 5.3.3, we are not enforcing the **algorithms** entry to be specified in the configuration.
When **algorithms** is not specified in the configuration, with the combination of jwks-rsa, it may lead to authorization bypass. 

### Am I affected?
You are affected by this vulnerability if all of the following conditions apply:

You are using express-jwt
AND 
You do not have **algorithms**  configured in your express-jwt configuration.
AND
You are using libraries such as jwks-rsa as the **secret**. 

### How to fix that?
Specify **algorithms** in the express-jwt configuration. The following is an example of a proper configuration

``` 
const checkJwt = jwt({
  secret: [REDACTED SECRET]
    rateLimit: true,
    jwksRequestsPerMinute: 5,
    jwksUri: `https://${DOMAIN}/.well-known/jwks.json`
  }),
  // Validate the audience and the issuer.
  audience: process.env.AUDIENCE,
  issuer: `https://${DOMAIN}/`,
  // restrict allowed algorithms
  algorithms: ['RS256']
}); 
```

### Will this update impact my users?
The fix provided in patch will not affect your users if you specified the algorithms allowed. The patch now makes **algorithms** a required configuration. 


### Credit
IST Group

sbom.name: jsonwebtoken

vulnerabilities.summary: jsonwebtoken unrestricted key type could lead to legacy keys usage
vulnerabilities.details:
# Overview

Versions `<=8.5.1` of `jsonwebtoken` library could be misconfigured so that legacy, insecure key types are used for signature verification. For example, DSA keys could be used with the RS256 algorithm. 

# Am I affected?

You are affected if you are using an algorithm and a key type other than the combinations mentioned below

| Key type |  algorithm                                    |
|----------|------------------------------------------|
| ec           | ES256, ES384, ES512                      |
| rsa          | RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512 |
| rsa-pss  | PS256, PS384, PS512                      |

And for Elliptic Curve algorithms:

| `alg` | Curve      |
|-------|------------|
| ES256 | prime256v1 |
| ES384 | secp384r1  |
| ES512 | secp521r1  |

# How do I fix it?

Update to version 9.0.0. This version validates for asymmetric key type and algorithm combinations. Please refer to the above mentioned algorithm / key type combinations for the valid secure configuration. After updating to version 9.0.0, If you still intend to continue with signing or verifying tokens using invalid key type/algorithm value combinations, you’ll need to set the `allowInvalidAsymmetricKeyTypes` option to `true` in the `sign()` and/or `verify()` functions.

# Will the fix impact my users?

There will be no impact, if you update to version 9.0.0 and you already use a valid secure combination of key type and algorithm. Otherwise,  use the  `allowInvalidAsymmetricKeyTypes` option  to `true` in the `sign()` and `verify()` functions to continue usage of invalid key type/algorithm combination in 9.0.0 for legacy compatibility.

Versions 4.2.1 and earlier of `jsonwebtoken` are affected by a verification bypass vulnerability. This is a result of weak validation of the JWT algorithm type, occuring when an attacker is allowed to arbitrarily specify the JWT algorithm.




## Recommendation

Update to version 4.2.2 or later.

vulnerabilities.summary: jsonwebtoken's insecure implementation of key retrieval function could lead to Forgeable Public/Private Tokens from RSA to HMAC
vulnerabilities.details:
# Overview

Versions `<=8.5.1` of `jsonwebtoken` library can be misconfigured so that passing a poorly implemented key retrieval function (referring to the `secretOrPublicKey` argument from the [readme link](https://github.com/auth0/node-jsonwebtoken#jwtverifytoken-secretorpublickey-options-callback)) will result in incorrect verification of tokens. There is a possibility of using a different algorithm and key combination in verification  than the one that was used to sign the tokens. Specifically, tokens signed with an asymmetric public key could be verified with a symmetric HS256 algorithm. This can lead to successful validation of forged tokens. 

# Am I affected?

You will be affected if your application is supporting usage of both symmetric key and asymmetric key in jwt.verify() implementation with the same key retrieval function. 

# How do I fix it?
 
Update to version 9.0.0.

# Will the fix impact my users?

There is no impact for end users

vulnerabilities.summary: jsonwebtoken vulnerable to signature validation bypass due to insecure default algorithm in jwt.verify()
vulnerabilities.details:
# Overview

In versions <=8.5.1 of jsonwebtoken library, lack of algorithm definition and a falsy secret or key in the `jwt.verify()` function can lead to signature validation bypass due to defaulting to the `none` algorithm for signature verification.

# Am I affected?
You will be affected if all the following are true in the `jwt.verify()` function:
- a token with no signature is received
- no algorithms are specified 
- a falsy (e.g. null, false, undefined) secret or key is passed 

# How do I fix it?
 
Update to version 9.0.0 which removes the default support for the none algorithm in the `jwt.verify()` method. 

# Will the fix impact my users?

There will be no impact, if you update to version 9.0.0 and you don’t need to allow for the `none` algorithm. If you need 'none' algorithm, you have to explicitly specify that in `jwt.verify()` options.

sbom.name: sanitize-html

vulnerabilities.details:
Affected versions of `sanitize-html` do not sanitize input recursively, which may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary Javascript.


## Recommendation

Update to version 1.4.3 or later.
The package sanitize-html before 2.7.1 are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) due to insecure global regular expression replacement logic of HTML comment removal.

vulnerabilities.summary: ApostropheCMS: Mutation-XSS / allowedTags bypass via literal `</textarea/>` solidus close
vulnerabilities.details: ### Summary A mutation-XSS / allowedTags bypass: when `textarea` (or `xmp`) is included in `allowedTags`, an input containing a literal `` (a solidus right after the RCDATA end-tag name) lets non-allowed markup such as `` pass through `sanitizeHtml()` **live and unescaped**, even though `img`/`onerror` are not in the allowlist. A spec-compliant browser executes the surviving handler — XSS. This is a literal-solidus variant that bypasses the two most recent fixes in this code area (CVE-2026-40186, CVE-2026-44990), both already applied in 2.17.5. The default configuration is not affected. ### Details `sanitize-html` emits the text content of HTML raw-text elements (`textarea`, `xmp`) without escaping. Two things combine: - **Parser differential:** on input, htmlparser2 does NOT recognize `` (solidus after the RCDATA end-tag name) as a close tag; it emits `` as a single raw-text node. - **Unescaped passthrough:** the `ontext` handler (`index.js` ~575-583) appends `textarea`/`xmp` content with `result += text` (no `escapeHtml`), assuming it is "already properly encoded" — true for entity-decoded content (what CVE-2026-40186 fixed) but false for this mis-tokenized literal close tag. A spec browser treats `` as a valid `textarea` close, so the following `` is parsed as a live element. The recent fixes addressed entity-encoding (CVE-2026-40186) and the `xmp` default (CVE-2026-44990); neither covers the literal-solidus mis-tokenization, so the raw passthrough still leaks. ### PoC ```js // npm i sanitize-html@2.17.5 parse5 && node poc.js const sanitizeHtml = require('sanitize-html'); const input = ''; const opts = { allowedTags: sanitizeHtml.defaults.allowedTags.concat(['textarea']) }; // img NOT allowed console.log(sanitizeHtml(input, opts)); // => // the survives live and unescaped console.log(sanitizeHtml(input)); // default config (no textarea allowed) => "" (safe) ``` Re-parsing the sanitized OUTPUT with **parse5** (the WHATWG HTML parser browsers/jsdom use) yields a **live ``** at `body` level (it escaped the textarea RCDATA, not inert text) → the `onerror` fires in a browser. Confirmed on 2.17.5 (Node v24). A canonical `poc.js` is attached. ### Impact Cross-site scripting (CWE-79). Requires `textarea` (or `xmp`) in `allowedTags` — a benign-looking, common addition in form builders, CMS, and rich-text editors. Adding a harmless tag that then enables XSS via *non-allowed* `img`/`onerror` breaks the sanitizer's core contract; the maintainers have fixed this class before (e.g. GHSA-9mrh). An attacker who can submit content rendered through such a configuration achieves stored/reflected XSS (cookie theft, session hijack). Severity Medium (default config is safe; user interaction to view the page). **Suggested fix:** route `textarea`/`xmp` content through `escapeHtml` instead of the raw passthrough, and/or fix the htmlparser2 `` RCDATA end-tag tokenization to match the WHATWG spec.

Apostrophe Technologies sanitize-html before 2.3.2 does not properly validate the hostnames set by the "allowedIframeHostnames" option when the "allowIframeRelativeUrls" is set to true, which allows attackers to bypass hostname whitelist for iframe element, related using an src value that starts with "/\\example.com".

vulnerabilities.summary: sanitize-html is vulnerable to XSS through incomprehensive sanitization
vulnerabilities.details: `sanitize-html` prior to version 2.0.0-beta is vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS). The `sanitizeHtml()` function in `index.js` does not sanitize content when using the custom `transformTags` option, which is intended to convert attribute values into text. As a result, malicious input can be transformed into executable code.

Apostrophe Technologies sanitize-html before 2.3.1 does not properly handle internationalized domain name (IDN) which could allow an attacker to bypass hostname whitelist validation set by the "allowedIframeHostnames" option.

Versions of the package sanitize-html before 2.12.1 are vulnerable to Information Exposure when used on the backend and with the style attribute allowed, allowing enumeration of files in the system (including project dependencies). An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to gather details about the file system structure and dependencies of the targeted server.

insights: CRITICAL: 2 critical vulnerabilities identified — immediate remediation required before next deployment.
HIGH RISK: 4 high-severity findings present. Schedule remediation within 7 days per SLA guidelines.
INJECTION CLUSTER: 6 injection-class vulnerabilities detected. Review all input validation and sanitisation across the codebase.
SSRF RISK: 1 Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability detected. Validate all outbound HTTP request URLs against a server-side allow-list.
DESERIALIZATION: 1 insecure deserialization sink detected. Never deserialize untrusted data with pickle, yaml.load, or ObjectInputStream.
SECRET EXPOSURE: 2 hardcoded credentials found. Rotate all affected credentials immediately and audit VCS history.
REPEATED PATTERNS: 1 root-cause vulnerability type with 1 additional occurrence. Fix the root cause in shared code to eliminate all occurrences.
ATTACK PATHS: 3 modeled attack paths identified (3 confirmed). Confirmed paths have validated source-to-sink evidence; candidate paths require manual validation before exploitability is established.
PIVOT POINTS: server.ts, infrastructure/docker-compose.yml, infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf are reachable from multiple attack chains — prioritize remediation of these vulnerabilities first.

SUPPLY CHAIN: 2 dependency packages with CVSS >= 7.0 detected. 3 vulnerable dependency packages have statically observed reachability evidence. This does not by itself prove runtime execution. Upgrade affected packages to patched versions before release.
COMPLIANCE RISK: 6 Critical/High findings require review against PCI DSS, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 applicability. Engage the security team for formal risk acceptance where required.

specification.document: CERT-In Technical Guidelines on SBOM, QBOM & CBOM, AIBOM and HBOM
specification.table: Table 8: Minimum Elements of QBOM & CBOM
specification.license: Government of India, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. Not a licence grant; cited by reference.
specification.dataset_label: CERT-In Technical Guidelines on SBOM, QBOM & CBOM, AIBOM and HBOM v2.0 (Table 8)

qbom.definition: CERT-In v2.0 Chapter 8.1, quoted from the pinned primary source: 'A Quantum Bill of Materials (QBOM) and a Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) are structured inventories that provide comprehensive visibility into an organization's cryptographic and quantum-related components. The QBOM focuses on components related to quantum computing and quantum-safe cryptography. It includes quantum algorithms, security frameworks, and related technologies, enabling organizations to maintain integrity, compliance, and resilience as they adopt post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) solutions.'
qbom.scope: This QBOM is produced by a static source-code analyser. It covers the Table 8 elements that a source inventory can state and marks the rest as NOT_OBSERVABLE_FROM_SOURCE with a reason. Elements describing a physical quantum device -- model, vendor, communication protocol, hardware, energy -- cannot be observed from source and are emitted as null by design, not by omission. A consumer should treat this as PARTIAL coverage of Table 8 and complete it from a device or procurement inventory.
qbom.status: CERT-In v2.0 Table 8 implementation, partial by construction: 5 of 11 minimum elements are observable from source and 6 describe physical quantum hardware that source analysis cannot see.

post_quantum_references.name: @types/cross-spawn
post_quantum_references.evidence: name matches a post-quantum cryptography term

element_coverage.note: Coverage is a property of the analyser, not of the scanned system. It does not improve when the codebase has more quantum code.

model_name.description: Provides a unique identifier for the quantum device or system, ensuring easy reference and distinction.
model_name.scope_note: Identifies a physical quantum device or system. A source scan observes code, not installed hardware, so no model name can be asserted.

version.description: Tracks version numbers and updates, including new features, security patches, and system enhancements.
version.scope_note: The version of a quantum DEVICE. Component versions are recorded under software_dependencies, which is a different element and must not be conflated with the device version.

vendor_origin.description: Records the manufacturer and origin of the quantum device, ensuring clarity in vendor communication, support, and maintenance.
vendor_origin.scope_note: Manufacturer and origin of physical quantum hardware, obtainable only from a device inventory or procurement record.

license_information.description: Documents the licensing terms and conditions for the quantum device, ensuring compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.
license_information.scope_note: Populated from the licences already resolved for inventoried software components. This covers the SOFTWARE side of the element; a hardware licence would need the device record.

cryptographic_asset.description: For a cryptographic asset, the minimum elements are those of Table 9, depending on the cryptographic asset type.
cryptographic_asset.scope_note: Cross-referenced from the Cryptographic Bill of Materials this tool already emits. The per-asset fields of Table 9 live there, not here, so this element points at that artifact rather than duplicating it.

classification_coverage.note: 0 of 1 assets could be classified; 1 could not and are reported as UNKNOWN rather than assumed safe.

value.table_9_fields: Per-asset CERT-In Table 9 minimum elements remain in the CBOM artifact; this element is the quantum-facing view.
value.source: Classified from this scan's own CBOM by scanner/crypto_quantum_analyzer. No external database consulted.

communication_protocol.description: Specifies the communication protocols used by the quantum device, ensuring seamless integration and compatibility with other systems.
communication_protocol.scope_note: Wire protocols between a quantum device and control infrastructure. Not present in source code.

hardware.description: Describes the hardware components that make up the quantum device, including the processor, simulators, networking components, and sensors required for quantum operations.
hardware.scope_note: Processor, simulator, networking and sensor inventory of a physical device. Explicitly a Hardware Bill of Materials subject, which is tracked separately as NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

software_dependencies.description: Describes the software elements interacting with the quantum hardware, including libraries, APIs, SDKs, and firmware updates.
software_dependencies.scope_note: Derived from the SBOM already produced for this scan.

environmental_impact.description: Tracks the environmental impact of the quantum system, including energy consumption and other sustainability factors.
environmental_impact.scope_note: Energy consumption and sustainability of quantum hardware. Requires operational measurement, not source analysis.

vulnerabilities_information.description: Information about known security vulnerabilities or weaknesses associated with the components, including severity ratings and references to security advisories or CVE identifiers.
vulnerabilities_information.scope_note: Derived from the advisories and findings of this scan, for the components this scan actually inventoried.

value.source: Findings of this scan only. No external vulnerability database was consulted for this element.

attestations.description: Digital signature for the QBOM to ensure authenticity and integrity.
attestations.scope_note: A SHA-256 content digest over the canonicalised inventory is computable and is emitted. It is a content digest, NOT a digital signature: no signing key is held, so no signature is claimed. The element's authenticity guarantee is therefore only partially satisfied, and that limit is recorded in the artifact.

value.covers: every field of this document except this attestations element: the specification block, scope, status, quantum_components, post_quantum_references, element_coverage, limits, and the complete value of all 10 other minimum elements
value.note: This is a content digest, not a signature. It establishes that the document has not changed since it was produced, including the inventory it records. It does NOT establish authenticity, because no signing key is held and no party vouches for the contents.

limits: Partial coverage of Table 8 by construction: 6 of 11 elements describe physical quantum hardware and cannot be observed from source.
The Attestations element is a SHA-256 content digest, NOT a digital signature. No signing key is held.
No external vulnerability database was consulted for the Vulnerabilities Information element; it reflects this scan only.
A Hardware Bill of Materials (Table 11) is a separate artifact and is NOT implemented. The Hardware element of Table 8 is correspondingly null.
A Quantum BOM that lists no quantum components is the correct output for a codebase with no quantum dependency. No component is ever synthesised.

qbom_pq.distinct_question: Which cryptographic assets in this source break under a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, and in what order should they be migrated? Distinct from the CERT-In Table 8 conformance document in Security_QBOM.qbom.json.

classification_rules.QUANTUM_VULNERABLE: Broken by Shor's algorithm. Applies to RSA, DSA, DH, ECDSA, ECDH and the Edwards curves -- including ed25519, which is vulnerable precisely BECAUSE it is strong.
classification_rules.QUANTUM_MARGIN_CRITICAL: Grover destroys the margin outright rather than reducing it. A 64-bit effective key such as DES or 3DES falls to roughly 32 bits, below any acceptable floor. Separate from QUANTUM_VULNERABLE because the mechanism is not Shor's and the migration advice differs: a 64-bit symmetric key must be replaced by one of adequate length, not by a PQC algorithm.
classification_rules.PQC: Already post-quantum: the ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA families, including their NIST parameter sets.
classification_rules.QUANTUM_IMPACT_ASSESSED: Reduced margin, not broken. Grover's algorithm halves the effective key length, so AES-128 becomes AES-64 equivalent. Not a migration trigger on its own.
classification_rules.UNKNOWN: The primitive could not be classified. This is NOT a safe result: it means the inventory cannot tell, and it is reported as its own category rather than folded into a low-risk bucket.

packs.document: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft): Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
packs.scope: Describes NIST's EXPECTED APPROACH to the transition and is meant to inform federal agencies, industry and standards bodies. It is an informative draft, not a FIPS mandate; its dates are NIST's expected approach, not a standard in force.
packs.hybrid_position: IR 8547 does not require hybrid operation; it points to FIPS 203/204/205 as standards that can and should be put into use now.
approved_pqc: SP 800-208 LMS/XMSS (single-tree use as specified there)

packs.document: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (CNSA 2.0) Cybersecurity Advisory
packs.scope: Applies to US National Security Systems (NSS) -- networks with classified information or otherwise critical to military and intelligence activities. For non-NSS systems it is a direction-of-travel reference, not a requirement.
packs.hybrid_position: Hybrid solutions may be allowed for interoperability, but the post-quantum component must itself be CNSA 2.0 compliant (CNSA 2.0 FAQ).

packs.document: BSI TR-02102-1: Cryptographic Mechanisms: Recommendations and Key Lengths (Kryptographische Verfahren: Empfehlungen und Schlüssellängen), Version 2026-01
packs.scope: German federal security authority guidance for new cryptographic deployments: recommendations with a stated 120-bit security level, not a legal mandate. TR-02102-2 records that solo classical key establishment is recommended only until the end of 2031 (TR-02102-1 section 2.1).
packs.hybrid_position: BSI intends to recommend quantum-safe procedures in HYBRID use with recommended classical procedures as suitable standards mature (TR-02102-2 section 3.1.3); hybridation is the expected migration mode.
approved_pqc: LMS (RFC 8554 / SP 800-208) -- stateful hash-based signatures long recommended by BSI (TR-02102, TR-03140)
Current quantum-safe key-agreement and signature recommendations: see TR-02102-1 itself (this pack does not transcribe the guideline's algorithm tables)

packs.document: Avis scientifique et technique de l'ANSSI sur la migration vers la cryptographie post-quantique (11 April 2022), with ANSSI views on the PQC transition -- 2023 follow up (21 December 2023)
packs.scope: French national cyber-security agency guidance shaping ANSSI security visas: a phased transition agenda and a hybridation recommendation, not a single calendar deadline.
packs.hybrid_position: ANSSI strongly emphasizes hybridation wherever post-quantum mitigation is needed in the short and medium term -- especially products aiming at confidentiality protection lasting beyond 2030. Hybrid is mandatory for phase-2 visas; phase 3 (after years of analysis, roughly post-2030) may make it optional.
approved_pqc: No closed list published: ANSSI accepts well-studied candidates subject to its assurance criteria and states selected algorithms may not exactly match NIST standards (2022 avis, section 10)

vocabulary.MIGRATE: The pack establishes a transition expectation for this class of algorithm: plan and execute migration within the pack's stated dates or phases.
vocabulary.REPLACE: The algorithm fails on its own terms -- broken or with its margin destroyed -- independently of quantum computing. Replace it; this is not a migration-to-PQC question.
vocabulary.ACCEPTABLE: The pack's published position does not require a change for this observation, given the parameters recorded by the scan.
vocabulary.ALIGNED: The observed algorithm belongs to a family or parameter set the pack approves or recommends for post-quantum use.
vocabulary.REVIEW: The observation cannot be mapped to a pack position: unclassified algorithm, parameter below or unconfirmable against the pack's rules, a pre-standardisation spelling, or a family the pack does not list. Human review required -- this is NOT a pass.

QUANTUM_VULNERABLE.note: Deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035 at the 112-bit security strength (common RSA, ECDSA/ECDH, FFDH sizes); the >=128-bit variants are disallowed after 2035. NIST states FIPS 203/204/205 can and should be put into use now.

QUANTUM_MARGIN_CRITICAL.note: Grover-depleted symmetric margin (DES/3DES class). NIST's few 112-bit-level symmetric standards are disallowed in 2030, and SP 800-131A retired 3DES for encryption before any quantum argument.

correlated_flows.title: Workflow / Approval / Duplicate Action Bypass
correlated_flows.description: Workflow-sensitive action appears without clear server-side approval/idempotency enforcement.
remediation: Enforce object-level authorization before repository/database access.
Validate tenant ownership in every data access path.
Use centralized authorization guards and regression tests.
Make workflow state transitions atomic and server-side enforced.

correlated_findings.pci_dss: Req 6.2.4 / Req 8 - Abuse prevention and authentication controls
correlated_findings.description: Enterprise static control matched: Abuse-Prone Endpoint Missing Rate-Limit Control.
remediation: Add server-side per-account/per-IP/per-tenant limits appropriate to the endpoint.
Add progressive backoff for login/OTP/reset and idempotency keys for payment or other duplicate-sensitive actions.
Return 429 on throttling, emit abuse metrics, and add burst/replay regression tests.

correlated_findings.title: Payment Duplicate Action / Missing Idempotency
correlated_findings.description: Abuse-prone payment endpoint appears without nearby rate-limit, replay, lockout, or idempotency controls.
remediation: Require an idempotency key for retryable payment or checkout requests.
Enforce idempotency atomically inside the server-side transaction so concurrent retries cannot create duplicate charges.
Bind the idempotency record to the authenticated account and operation parameters; reject key reuse with a different payload.
Add tests for retries, concurrent submissions, timeout replay, and mismatched idempotency keys.

indicators.title: OTP Brute Force Missing Rate Limit
indicators.snippet: /rest/2fa/verify
indicators.description: Abuse-prone endpoint lacks clear rate-limit, replay, lockout, or idempotency controls.
indicators.business_impact: Attackers can automate brute-force, replay, duplicate transaction, coupon, OTP, or reset workflows leading to account takeover, fraud, and service abuse.
remediation: Add per-user/IP/tenant rate limits.
Add lockout/backoff for login, OTP and reset workflows.
Use idempotency keys for payment and state-changing actions.
Monitor and alert on abuse patterns.

source_indicators.title: OTP Brute Force Missing Rate Limit
source_indicators.description: Abuse-prone endpoint lacks clear rate-limit, replay, lockout, or idempotency controls.
source_indicators.business_impact: Attackers can automate brute-force, replay, duplicate transaction, coupon, OTP, or reset workflows leading to account takeover, fraud, and service abuse.
remediation: Add per-user/IP/tenant rate limits.
Add lockout/backoff for login, OTP and reset workflows.
Use idempotency keys for payment and state-changing actions.
Monitor and alert on abuse patterns.

ssdf_alignment.method: Per-practice EVIDENCE alignment against a produced artifact. No practice identifier is attached to any finding: a scanner cannot evidence an organisational practice, and asserting one would convert absence into assurance.
ssdf_alignment.scope_note: Limited to practices confirmed present in SSDF v1.1. PO.6 and PW.10 belong to a later EO 14144 revision and are excluded.

practices.practice: PO.1: Define Security Requirements for Software Development
practices.name: Define Security Requirements for Software Development
practices.rationale: Organisational policy practice. Establishing and maintaining security requirements for a development infrastructure is an organisational commitment; no scan output can evidence it.

practices.name: Implement Roles and Responsibilities
practices.rationale: Roles and responsibilities, including role-based training. Not observable from source or artifact.

practices.name: Supporting Toolchains
practices.rationale: The practice is about establishing and using supporting toolchains. V11 being installed is not evidence that the organisation established or uses one as SSDF intends.
Practice identifier confirmed in v1.1; purpose not confirmed in this session.

practices.practice: PO.5: Implement and Maintain Secure Environments for Software Development
practices.name: Implement and Maintain Secure Environments for Software Development
practices.rationale: Maintaining secure development environments is an environment property, not a source property.

practices.practice: PS.1: Protect All Forms of Code from Unauthorized Access and Tampering
practices.name: Protect All Forms of Code from Unauthorized Access and Tampering
practices.rationale: Secret scanning and code-integrity findings are evidence that software components are being checked for unauthorised access and tampering. This is partial evidence for the practice, not proof of it.

practices.practice: PS.2: Provide a Mechanism for Verifying Software Release Integrity
practices.name: Provide a Mechanism for Verifying Software Release Integrity
practices.rationale: Runtime artifact integrity plus the emitted VEX and CycloneDX documents constitute a mechanism for verifying release integrity.

practices.practice: PS.3: Archive and Protect Each Software Release
practices.name: Archive and Protect Each Software Release
practices.rationale: An SBOM with CycloneDX provenance output is the archival and provenance record for a release (PS.3.2 collects provenance data).

practices.practice: PW.1: Design Software to Meet Security Requirements and Mitigate Security Risks
practices.name: Design Software to Meet Security Requirements and Mitigate Security Risks
practices.rationale: Designing software to meet security requirements is a design-time activity. A static scanner runs after the design exists and holds no design artefact, so no evidence can be produced either way.

practices.practice: PW.2: Review the Software Design to Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
practices.name: Review the Software Design to Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
practices.rationale: Reviewing a design against requirements needs the design and the requirements. Neither is in scope for a code scanner.
Practice identifier confirmed in v1.1; purpose not confirmed in this session.

practices.practice: PW.5: Create Source Code by Adhering to Secure Coding Practices
practices.name: Create Source Code by Adhering to Secure Coding Practices
practices.rationale: SAST and taint detections are evidence of secure-coding practice, with the caveat that absence of findings is not evidence of secure code.

practices.practice: RV.1: Identify and Confirm Vulnerabilities on an Ongoing Basis
practices.name: Identify and Confirm Vulnerabilities on an Ongoing Basis
practices.rationale: Live KEV and EPSS feeds, vulnerability-age and outbreak state are ongoing vulnerability identification and confirmation.

practices.practice: RV.2: Assess, Prioritize, and Remediate Vulnerabilities
practices.name: Assess, Prioritize, and Remediate Vulnerabilities
practices.rationale: Reachability-aware prioritisation, exploitability fusion and the release-readiness gates are assessment, prioritisation and remediation planning.
Practice identifier confirmed in v1.1; purpose not confirmed in this session.

compliance_summary_detail.caveat: counts are framework-presence over grouped findings, not coverage. Three frameworks are applied to every finding by GENERIC_MAPPING, so a count of 102 for NIST 800-53 means 102 findings carry *a* NIST control id, not that 102 distinct control decisions were made.

asvs_summary.semantics: Ratios describe reachability into ASVS's catalogue, not compliance. ASVS is a verification standard: most requirements are verification activities, so most are unreachable by design.

unreferenced_cwe.CWE-347: ASVS v4.0.3 does not cite this CWE in its enumeration.
unreferenced_cwe.CWE-943: ASVS v4.0.3 does not cite this CWE in its enumeration.
unreferenced_cwe.CWE-321: ASVS v4.0.3 does not cite this CWE in its enumeration.

free_ai_summary.legal_status: Committee report. NOT a binding RBI direction, Master Direction or regulation. Presenting it as an obligation would overstate it.
free_ai_summary.semantics: Ratios describe reachability into a committee report addressed to Indian financial-sector regulated entities. They are NOT compliance, NOT a regulatory obligation, and NOT a statement that the framework applies to this corpus: applicability to a given codebase is never established by this tool. 19 of 26 recommendations ask for organisational acts that no source scan can observe, so full coverage is impossible by construction.

sans_summary.dataset: SANS Critical AI Security Guidelines v1.4 (2026-03)
sans_summary.alignment: Aligned with the OWASP AI Exchange
sans_summary.guidance_status: Guidance from a training vendor. NOT a regulation, not a certification requirement, and not a binding standard.
sans_summary.semantics: Ratios describe reachability into SANS guidance. They are NOT compliance and NOT a certification score. Control identifiers are locally assigned by this project because the guidelines number nothing; see id_origin. A majority of the controls concern governance, hosting and oversight that a source scan cannot observe, so full coverage is impossible by construction.

wstg_summary.dataset: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide v4.2
wstg_summary.status: OWASP guidance. A TESTING guide, not a regulation, certification requirement, or vulnerability taxonomy. A mapping means the finding is the kind of weakness a test case looks for; it does NOT mean this scan performed that test.
wstg_summary.semantics: Ratios describe reachability into WSTG guidance. They are NOT conformance and NOT a certification score. A WSTG test case is a procedure against a running application; mapping a finding to one does not mean the procedure was performed. Cases a source scan cannot discharge are reported separately rather than counted as covered.
wstg_summary.licence_gap: The WSTG checkout carries no root LICENSE file, so no licence is asserted for the identifiers and titles embedded here. Treat redistribution as an open question until the terms are read from an authoritative source.
